Strengthen storage, append-only history, and durability primitives (compaction, integrity, gc, export/import)
History chain integrity gates stay green; gc, compact, redact, and repair flows verified on large workspaces; no open data-loss classes.

## Charter
Living capability epic for storage, append-only history, and data durability: TOON item files, per-item history streams (hash-chained JSONL), checkpoints, gc, compaction, export/import, and format_version gating.

## Scope
- In: item-store write paths, history chain integrity (repair/redact/compact), gc scopes (locks/checkpoints/embeddings), backup/restore, format migrations.
- Out: concurrency/locking semantics (pm-dj98 owns races and atomicity), search index storage (pm-ydp6).

## Invariants this epic guards
- History is append-only and hash-chained; appendLineAtomic is the only writer (see pm-y2ml docs).
- Items must survive strict→lenient TOON decode fallback (2026-05-24 recovery precedent).
- pm health history_drift must stay at 0 across 1400+ items.

## Status
20 closed children (compact snapshot, history-compact bulk + policy, gc scopes, restore hardening). Open as a living backlog — no open children at 2026-07-04; new durability work lands here.

Full all-status backlog review found the append-only-proof guarantee is complete for items (restore-to-version pm-9lc, file recovery pm-g6qd, per-stream --verify, workspace drift scan) but not for workspace-level state. Two new children:
- **pm-klo8** — workspace-scoped audit history stream: schema/config/profile/init/extension-state mutations get the same append-only hash-chained JSONL treatment as items (coordinate with pm-bgcu locking; feeds pm-e200).

value.text: Immutable-proof review 2026-07-18: the live tracker has 30,491 activity entries across 1,874 streams; every one of the 1,866 current items has at least one recorded event, and validation reports zero missing streams, hash mismatches, chain mismatches, or drifted items. Mutation-op inventory includes create/update/claim/release/close, annotations, linked artifacts, test runs, plans, compact/repair/redact, and even edit/delete operations as recorded events. Remaining guarantee extensions are already individually tracked: pm-klo8 for workspace singleton state, pm-9yfo for contract-enumerated mutation completeness, pm-4e12 for atomic multi-entity commits, pm-g5sx for branch-safe merge/reconciliation, pm-3z0k for portable attestations, and pm-u14c for principal signatures. Point-in-time non-mutating read pm-hib1 and restore/recovery foundations are shipped. No new history item needed.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Immutable-history assessment 2026-07-25, written against the standing requirement that every mutating action be permanently recorded, that the record be unalterable after the fact, and that any item be restorable to any prior version.

Recorded: every mutating CLI and SDK action appends to a per-item append-only JSONL stream; workspace-scoped mutations (schema, config, profile, init) have their own hash-chained audit stream; the stream is content-addressed and chained, so an edit to any entry breaks verification downstream; history --verify --strict-exit makes that check a gate rather than a report; redaction, repair, and compaction all exist as governed, recorded operations rather than as file edits. Restoration exists in both directions: point-in-time read projection (get --at) reconstructs historical state without mutating, and restore replays a stream to recover a deleted or missing item, with hash validation.

Two properties are asserted rather than proven, and both are filed. Completeness - that no mutating path can skip the append - is asserted by convention today; pm-9yfo makes it a contract-driven test enumerated from the action table, which is the only form that survives new commands being added. Independent verifiability - that a third party can confirm the record without trusting this tooling - needs the detached attestation bundle in pm-3z0k, complemented by per-entry author signatures in pm-u14c so that the answer to who recorded this is as strong as the answer to whether it was altered.

One honest limitation to record rather than paper over: immutability here is tamper-evident, not tamper-proof. A party with write access to the repository can rewrite a stream; what they cannot do is rewrite it without the chain revealing the rewrite, provided a verifier holds an earlier anchor. That is why the attestation bundle matters more than any additional in-repository control - it moves the anchor outside the trust boundary. The acknowledgment flow shipped this pass is the correct shape for the same reason: unknown-author events are dispositioned by appending an audited acknowledgment, never by attributing authorship retroactively.

The remaining practical risk is growth rather than integrity: 33.5k history entries across 1,983 streams today, with compaction available but its cadence unautomated. That is pm-o79o, and it becomes load-bearing at the decade-shaped workspace the outcome milestone targets.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Durability and time-travel contract: every mutating CLI, SDK, MCP, package, automation, and repair action appends a canonical event containing event ID, item/workspace identity, schema version, actor/harness/session provenance, causal parents, timestamp plus monotonic ordering data, operation payload, prior-state/hash commitment, and resulting-state commitment. State is a deterministic fold; any version is restored by selecting a causal/time/event boundary and replaying from the nearest verified content-addressed snapshot. Segment logs and Merkle roots bound verification and replication cost, while periodic snapshots, indexes, and compaction manifests accelerate reads without deleting the authoritative chain. Corrections, redactions, migrations, normalization, conflict resolution, and rollback are new signed/hashed events that preserve the original fact and disclose the transformed view; destructive overwrite is never a repair mechanism. Verify crash consistency, truncated writes, duplicate/reordered events, hash gaps, schema evolution, cross-branch merges, clock skew, archive export/import, multi-decade cryptographic agility, and loss/recovery drills. Expose proof receipts for current hash, replay boundary, snapshot ancestry, omitted segments, verification status, and exact restore command through SDK-first contracts, with streaming NDJSON for shell tooling and bounded summaries for agents.
